cohort: The study included 1,517,106 subjects with an average age of 30.56 years, all of whom had a previous vaginal delivery.
finding: A J-shaped non-linear relationship was found between interpregnancy interval after vaginal delivery and preterm birth, with IPIs of <= 11 months and >= 24 months associated with an increased risk compared to 18-23 months.
mod_finding: The study specifically focused on interpregnancy intervals following a vaginal delivery, revealing a J-shaped relationship where both short (<= 11 months) and long (>= 24 months) intervals after vaginal delivery are associated with an increased risk of preterm birth.
